_why: The golden hash of the SHIPPED home page. Any phase not intended to change the
run must reproduce `outIndexSha256` exactly. Re-record it only after reading the
out/index.html diff by hand, and NEVER to make a red check go green.
Pinned at the tree it was measured on, per the standing rule that the number and
the sha move together. `runSourceSha256` is here so a mismatch tells you WHICH
side moved: if the source sha still matches but the output sha does not, the
build changed, not the page.
`commit` is the tree that produces `runSourceSha256`, and verify-portfolio
asserts that pairing on every run. This field named Phase 0 while the numbers
beside it were Phase 1's until 2026-08-06, and nothing went red because nothing
looked.
ORDER FIXES IT: --rebaseline writes HEAD, so if the code change is still
uncommitted it records the PARENT of the commit the baseline lands in, and the
field must then be corrected by hand. Commit the code FIRST and re-baseline
second and HEAD *is* the tree that produces `runSourceSha256` — right by
construction, no hand edit, which is how this entry was recorded.
The env matters, and `buildEnv` below is DERIVED from the env this hash was
actually taken under rather than typed beside it. It used to be a hand-kept
literal that --rebaseline never rewrote, and on the move to ayush-yadav.com it
went on asserting NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/Portfolio-2.0 while the numbers next to
it were measured at the root. Nothing reads this field, which is exactly why it
could drift; it is now written from DEPLOY_ENV on every re-baseline.
Every test:e2e:* script rebuilds with NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH= (empty) and re-runs
build-home.mjs, overwriting out/index.html, so this hash is taken under the
deploy configuration before any e2e step runs. Since the deploy base path is now
also empty the two builds agree — the post-smoke out/index.html was measured
byte-identical to this hash — but that is two settings coinciding rather than a
property, so the ordering is unchanged.
Determinism was proven, not assumed: two consecutive builds at this tree produced
byte-identical output, and the result also matched an out/ built in an earlier
session. build-home.mjs and build-nameplate.mjs carry no new Date(), Date.now(),
toISOString, randomUUID or Math.random, and out/index.html carries no chunk hashes.
_closure: The hash certifies ONE file; the run's dependency closure is much larger, and
deleting a piece of it reproduces the hash byte-for-byte while breaking the live
page. These are the floors verify-portfolio.mjs asserts separately.
Sizes are floors, not equalities: a re-subset font or a retrained model should
not fail the gate, but an empty or truncated file must.
